results.title: What’s the most frustrating part of your business?
results.content: # What’s the most frustrating part of your business? As a business owner, I find converting prospects really hard and frustrating. Also, as business owners, what’s the most frustrating part of your business you wish someone could fix forever? - Not having enough customers to cover up the expenses we incurred and it might affect the business financial stability so I guess it would be better if I track it in fina money, copilot or tracky. - Not having enough customers to cover up the expenses we incurred and it might affect the business financial stability so I guess it would be better if I track it in fina money, copilot or tracky. - All the added tax filing/payment requirements, red tape dealing with some things, and sometimes waiting for invoices to be paid. - Problem is that there are little to no new business within my region to explore opportunities with. Established business in my region won't change their product offerings hence it's the same seasonal items year by year. Although I keep on cold emailing them in hopes that my sourcing business can open up a lot of new opportunities and business ventures but it's clear as day that they do not need a new business approach. In the end I have to grow my business through doing my own brand and develop a market for my products. Often they are corporate zombies, thinking they are entitled to whatever they demand…(sorry that’s not how it works). - Dealing with flaky clients sucks. I do a lot of online sales and the way USPS has crashed and burned this year is remarkable. - Ups, usps Seems like once a box is over 30 lbs, we see a severe lag in delivery or a completely lost package. We stopped shipping usps flat rate boxes over 40# last month, and that seems to help a bit. Those boxes are good for up to 70 lbs. Frustrating when people bitch about rich people, pay raises, and working conditions and then fail to do their own jobs to the standard they were hired for.

results.title: Fina Money is rated "Great" with 3.9 / 5 on Trustpilot
results.content:
If you’re thinking about using Fina Money, please reconsider. There are plenty of legitimate financial service providers out there, but this one is not one of them. I lost both time and money dealing with them, and I would hate for anyone else to go through the same situation. This company should be investigated for misleading and unethical practices.  
  
Avoid Fina Money at all costs. Save yourself the stress, frustration, and potential financial loss. [...] After signing up, I was charged unexpected fees that were never clearly explained. When I tried to reach out to customer service, I either received automated responses or no reply at all. It became clear that they have no intention of actually providing the services they advertise. Instead, they seem focused on collecting money and then disappearing behind vague excuses and broken promises.  
  
What’s worse is how unprofessional and inconsistent their communication is. Every email or message feels copy-pasted, and no one takes responsibility for the issues. I also found multiple reports from other customers describing the exact same experience, which only confirms that this is a pattern — not an isolated case. [...] I'm running a small business and as many new businesses do I mixed my personal and business finances pretty heavily for the first year or so. Eventually I started to get a bit more organized, but even so I had hundreds of transactions to sort through with no system in place whatsoever. Fina has rules in place plus AI to sort through even the most disorganized users finances ie. me. I separated out personal and business expenses, got some awesome insights into where money is being spent, made cool visualizations that automatically update. I don't know the team behind Fina but when I reached out about something it was a real person, plus they have a form to submit requests for features, and bugs. Not the first financial software I have tried, I definitely recommend them!!
